data.headline: Amazon, Samsung see AI driving sales, chip demand
data.summary: STORY: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy says artificial intelligence could help cloud computing unit Amazon Web Services achieve $600 billion in annual sales.The outlook came in an internal all-hands meeting on Tuesday, with his comments reviewed by Reuters. Jassy said with what's happening in AI, AWS has a chance to "at least double" his previous $300 billion revenue estimate. The cloud provider booked almost $129 billion in sales in 2025, up 19% on the year.Jassy’s projection suggests an average growth rate of nearly 17% every year for the next decade.Wall Street has balked at Amazon's planned commitment of $200 billion in capital expenditure for AI this year, sending its shares down sharply.But Jassy said the spending was carefully planned, and would pay off.Samsung Electronics also sees AI continuing to drive strong demand for chips this year.Co-CEO Jun Young-hyun said Wednesday the company expects a "favorable business environment due to the increasing demand for AI and the resulting continued shortage of memory supply."Roaring demand for semiconductors for AI data centers has curbed memory chip shipments to other sectors, allowing Samsung and rivals to sharply hike prices. That has seen shares in the firm skyrocket to record highs, up around 70% since the start of the year.
